seoTitle: How to Host a Website on Google Workspace (Google Sites)
metaDescription: Learn how to host your website using Google Sites within Google Workspace in 2026, starting from a blank page or a ready-made template.
intro: Google Sites gives Workspace users a straightforward way to build and host a website without needing separate hosting or coding skills. This guide covers how to get started with either a blank site or one of Google's templates.

steps.heading: Review your Workspace access
steps.body: Confirm your Google Workspace plan includes Google Sites, which is available across most standard and business editions.

steps.heading: Start with a blank site
steps.body: Choose the blank site option if you want full control over layout and design from the very first page.

steps.heading: Or start from a template
steps.body: Google Sites offers pre-built templates you can customize, which is faster if you want a polished look without designing from scratch.

steps.heading: Build out your pages
steps.body: Add pages, text, images, and embedded content, arranging your site's navigation to match how visitors should move through it.

steps.heading: Publish and host on Google Workspace
steps.body: Once your site is ready, publish it and connect a custom domain if you want it to appear under your own web address instead of Google's default one.

faq.question: Is Google Sites free with Google Workspace?
faq.answer: Google Sites is included with most Google Workspace plans at no extra cost, though storage and advanced features can depend on your edition.

faq.question: Can I use my own domain with a Google Sites website?
faq.answer: Yes, you can connect a custom domain you own to your Google Sites page instead of using Google's default site address.

faq.question: Is it better to start with a blank site or a template?
faq.answer: Templates save time and offer a professional starting point, while a blank site is better if you want complete design flexibility.

faq.question: Can multiple people in my organization edit the same site?
faq.answer: Yes, Google Sites supports collaborative editing, so team members with the right permissions can update the site together.
